# 1 Enoch Chapter 60 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** In the year five hundred, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the life of Enoch: in that parable I saw how a mighty earthquake caused the heaven of heavens to quake, and the host of the Most High and the angels — a thousand thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand — were troubled with great trouble.

**2** And the Head of Days sat on the throne of his glory, and the angels and the righteous stood all around him.

**3** And a great trembling seized me, and fear took hold of me, and my loins gave way, and my reins dissolved, and I fell upon my face.

**4** And Michael sent another angel from among the holy ones who raised me up; and when he had raised me, my spirit returned, for I had not been able to endure the sight of this host, and the commotion and the quaking of heaven.

**5** And Michael said to me: Why are you troubled by such a vision? Until this day has lasted the day of his mercy, and he has been merciful and long-suffering toward those who dwell on the earth.

**6** But when the day, the power, the punishment, and the judgment come — which the Lord of Spirits has prepared for those who do not worship the righteous law, and for those who deny the righteous judgment, and for those who take his name in vain — that day is prepared: a covenant for the elect, but an inquisition for sinners.

**7** And on that day two monsters were parted: a female monster named Leviathan, to dwell in the abysses of the ocean over the fountains of the waters;

**8** and the male is named Behemoth, who occupied with his breast a waste wilderness named Duidain, to the east of the garden where the elect and righteous dwell — where my grandfather was taken up, the seventh from Adam, the first man whom the Lord of Spirits made.

**9** And I asked the other angel to show me the power of those monsters — how they were parted on one day and cast, the one into the abysses of the sea, and the other to the dry land of the wilderness.

**10** And he said to me: You, son of man, seek here to know what is secret.

**11** And the other angel who went with me and showed me what was hidden told me what is first and last in the heaven above, and beneath the earth in the depths, and at the ends of the heaven, and on the foundations of heaven.

**12** And the chambers of the winds, and how the winds are divided and weighed, and how the portals of the winds are counted, each according to the power of the wind, and the power of the lights of the moon, and according to the power that is fitting; and the divisions of the stars according to their names, and how all the divisions are apportioned.

**13** And the thunders according to the places where they fall, and all the divisions made among the lightnings that they may flash; and their host, that they may at once obey.

**14** For the thunder has places of rest, and a period is assigned to it. And the thunder and the lightning are inseparable — though not one and undivided, they both go together through the spirit and do not separate.

**15** For when the lightning lightens, the thunder utters its voice, and the spirit enforces a pause during the peal and divides equally between them; for the treasury of their peals is like the sand, and each one of them as it peals is restrained with a bridle and turned back by the power of the spirit, and pushed forward according to the many quarters of the earth.

**16** And the spirit of the sea is masculine and strong; and according to the might of his strength he draws it back with a rein, and in like manner it is driven forward and dispersed among all the mountains of the earth.

**17** And the spirit of the hoarfrost is his own angel, and the spirit of hail is a good angel.

**18** And the spirit of snow has forsaken his chambers on account of his strength — there is a special spirit in it, and that which ascends from it is like smoke, and its name is frost.

**19** And the spirit of the mist is not united with them in their chambers, but it has a special chamber; for its course is glorious both in light and in darkness, and in winter and in summer, and in its chamber is an angel.

**20** And the spirit of the dew has its abode at the ends of heaven, and is connected with the chambers of the rain; its course is in winter and in summer; and the clouds of dew and the clouds of the mist are connected, and the one gives to the other.

**21** And when the spirit of the rain goes forth from its chamber, the angels come and open the chamber and lead it forth; and when it is diffused over the whole earth it unites with the water that is upon the earth.

**22** And whenever it unites with the water that is upon the earth...

**23** For the waters are for those who dwell upon the earth; for they are nourishment for the earth from the Most High who is in heaven. Therefore there is a measure for the rain, and the angels take it in charge.

**24** And these things I saw toward the Garden of the Righteous.

**25** And the angel of peace who was with me said: These two monsters, prepared in accordance with the greatness of God, shall feed...

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Ge'ez text. Ch. 60 is the most complex chapter in the Parables, combining a heavenly throne vision (vv. 1–6), the Leviathan and Behemoth cosmogony (vv. 7–9, 24–25), and a detailed meteorological treatise (vv. 10–23). V. 25 is fragmentary. 'Duidain' is preserved as a proper place name. The 'year 500' locates this as Noah's era (Gen 5:32).*
